---
title: "Lab 03 — Regression for description and prediction"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
face <- read_csv("data/face.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    d.share = d.votes / (d.votes + r.votes),
    r.share = r.votes / (d.votes + r.votes),
    diff.share = d.share - r.share
  )
fit <- lm(diff.share ~ d.comp, data = face)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab03", title = "Regression for description and prediction", open = "q4")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "The slope of the Democratic vote margin on the competence rating is about…",
  q2 = "A fitted value is…",
  q3 = "Which use of the line is honest?",
  q4 = "Why is a prediction at a competence score far outside this sample risky?"
)
```

## What you will do

Read one OLS slope as description, not as an effect of changing a candidate's face. Then download the `.txt`.

```{r coef-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=2}
coef(fit)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("0.66. A competence rating 0.1 higher goes with a vote margin about 0.066 higher.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.66. A competence rating one point higher goes with a vote margin 66 percentage points higher."),
  answer("1. The rating determines the vote."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("The vote margin the line predicts at a given competence rating.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The causal effect for that candidate."),
  answer("The residual."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("In this sample, higher competence ratings go with a higher Democratic vote margin.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The regression proves that changing a face would change the vote."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "The line was fit inside the observed ratings.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
